name: family-vote-aggregation
rationale: Lead #4 from the 2026-09-14 report, now the best-evidenced open lead this pipeline has. That run instrumented the agreement gate over 15,286 candles and established a measured fact: across all 2,998 candles where all five sub-signals expressed an opinion, they NEVER reached 4-of-5 directional agreement, and the composite never left [0.3359, 0.6548]. The recorded cause is that the two families are near-mechanically opposed -- price above its moving averages is usually also high in its Bollinger band -- so the split is systematically 2-vs-3 or 3-vs-2 and the weighted mean cancels. The structural defect behind that is double-counting: compute_btc_target takes a weighted mean over five INDIVIDUAL sub-signals, three of which (SMA cross, EMA cross, MACD histogram) are near-duplicates of one another computed off the same price series, and two of which (RSI, Bollinger %B) are likewise near-duplicates. Averaging correlated votes treats them as independent evidence and understates the family that happens to have fewer members. The arithmetic is concrete: with REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT 1.0 and TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT 0.25, a fully-warmed point gives the reversion family 2 x 1.0 = 2.0 of realised weight against the trend family's 3 x 0.25 = 0.75 -- an effective 2.67:1 ratio, not the 4:1 the two constants were chosen (PR #12, 2026-09-09) to express. This hypothesis collapses each family to ONE vote (the unweighted mean of its available members) and then applies the existing 1.0 / 0.25 family weights to those two votes, so the intended 4:1 dominance is realised exactly and correlated members stop inflating their family's count. It is deliberately NOT a new weight value -- the two constants are untouched -- so it does not repeat mean-reversion-weighted-subsignals, trend-weighted-subsignals, trend-weight-half or ta-weight-085-signal-amplitude, all of which changed a gain and none of which can change how many votes a family casts. Expected direction on turnover is upward (the dominant family's swings are no longer diluted by three opposing trend votes), which keeps it clear of the promotion rule's 50%-of-baseline trade-count floor -- the criterion that rejected both of 2026-09-14's improving variants. Risk to watch and report honestly: if the realised composite band does NOT widen, the cancellation is not a counting artifact and lead #4 is answered negatively, which is itself worth recording.
code_change_summary: In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), change ONLY the aggregation step that turns the collected sub-signals into ta_normalized. Today each sub-signal is pushed onto `sub_signals: Vec<(f64, f64)>` as (value, family_weight) and ta_normalized is the weight-normalised mean over all five. Replace that with a two-stage family aggregation: (1) collect the reversion-family sub-signal VALUES (RSI, Bollinger %B) into one Vec<f64> and the trend-family sub-signal VALUES (SMA cross, EMA cross, MACD histogram) into another, using exactly the same per-sub-signal formulas, the same Some/None availability guards, and the same sma > 0.0 / ema > 0.0 / bb_middle > 0.0 fallbacks as today -- do not change how any individual sub-signal is computed; (2) reduce each non-empty family to a single vote equal to the UNWEIGHTED arithmetic mean of its available members; (3) compute ta_normalized as the weighted mean of the family votes present, using REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT for the reversion vote and TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT for the trend vote, dividing by the sum of the weights of the families actually present. A family with no available members contributes neither a vote nor its weight, exactly as an absent sub-signal contributes nothing today. If BOTH families are empty (full warmup), return None exactly as the current empty-sub_signals guard does. Leave REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT = 1.0 and TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT = 0.25 at their current values, leave damped_cross and CROSS_SATURATION untouched, and leave the sentiment combination `ta_normalized * ta_weight + sentiment_normalized * sentiment_weight` and its final clamp exactly as they are. Update the function's doc comment and the NOTE comments on both weight constants to state that the weights now apply to FAMILY votes rather than to individual sub-signals, and why (correlated members within a family were double-counted, making the realised ratio 2.67:1 rather than the intended 4:1). Add unit tests in the same module: (a) a fully-warmed point where all five sub-signals are available, asserting ta_normalized equals (reversion_mean * 1.0 + trend_mean * 0.25) / 1.25 and NOT the old five-term weighted mean; (b) a point with only reversion members available, asserting the result equals the reversion mean combined with sentiment (trend family absent contributes no weight); (c) the mirror case with only trend members available; (d) a warmup point with no indicator values at all, asserting None. Instrument and REPORT (via stderr logging or a scratch harness -- do not add a field to BacktestReport for this) the realised min/max/sd of ta_normalized over the evaluated window for both the baseline formula and the new one, so the report can state whether the composite band actually widened from the 2026-09-14 measurement of [0.3359, 0.6548].
constraints: This hypothesis DOES modify TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's body. That is permitted under experiments/hypotheses/README.md's '`compute_btc_target` may be modified' section, but ONLY on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch, and it MUST be reported explicitly so the coordinator flags it in any PR description.
MUST NOT change compute_btc_target's SIGNATURE. Only its body may change.

MUST NOT change any individual sub-signal formula, the damped_cross helper, CROSS_SATURATION, the numeric values of REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT or TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, the sentiment combine and its clamp, apply_zone, sticky_target, allocation_delta_to_order, the lot-size check, the orders_below_min counting arm, the RiskManager call sequence, or the fee logic. Only the aggregation from sub-signals to ta_normalized may change.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including every existing compute_btc_target_* unit test. Update an expected value only where the new aggregation legitimately changes it, and do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass.

MUST NOT fit anything on the holdout window, or on any window at all. This change introduces no new tunable constant; if a new constant seems needed, that is a result to report, not a value to retune mid-run.
MUST NOT change src/signal/engine.rs's broadcast cadence or anything about live scheduling.

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body and therefore changes the allocation target the live engine acts on.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the order-submission mechanics themselves.
